_comment: THE FLORA ROSTER — NAMING DECOMPOSES, IT DOES NOT ADD (docs/plan_flora_roster.md §2, the ruling this whole file rests on). A roster entry says what a tile's EXISTING forage capacity IS MADE OF; it never adds capacity on top. MixedWoodland's 190 (labor_config.json -> forage.capacity_by_biome) becomes named shares — hazel + oak mast + berry — that still sum to 190. The shares are DERIVED, never authored per tile: share(species, biome) = weight(species, biome) / SUM of the weights of every species hosting that biome, and patch_capacity(species, tile) = share x forage.capacity_by_biome[tile.biome]. Because the shares are normalized they sum to 1 BY CONSTRUCTION, so a tile's total can never drift from capacity_by_biome and adding a species to a biome DILUTES the others rather than inflating the tile. This file changes NO capacity — the host_biomes normalization makes that structural (see _comment_host_biomes), not a tuning promise. It DOES now change yield, but only for a patch a Cultivate/Sow assignment has COMMITTED to one species: an uncommitted (wild) patch still gathers the whole basket at labor_config's flat forage.provisions_per_biomass, so rung 1 is bit-identical to pre-roster (see _comment_yield). Keyed on TerrainType (the 38 biomes), NOT on FoodModule (the 10 buckets): fauna keys host_biomes off FoodModule because an animal RANGES over a region, but a plant IS its tile, and the buckets are too coarse to say 'this wants floodplain silt, not any wetland'. FoodModule is untouched — it still decides what KIND of gathering a tile offers, and its seasonal_weight.
_comment_coverage: COVERAGE MUST BE TOTAL OVER THE NON-ZERO FORAGE BIOMES, and must touch none of the zeros. validate_against_forage() rejects (a) any biome with a NON-ZERO forage.capacity_by_biome that NO species hosts — a tile whose food has no name — and (b) any species hosting a biome whose capacity is ZERO — claiming ground that carries no forage. That strict pair is the same 'zero must be stated, never defaulted' discipline capacity_by_biome itself enforces, and it is what forces BREADTH BEFORE DEPTH: F1 cannot ship 'a couple of species', it must ship a complete-but-coarse roster (13 broad staple families, each hosting many biomes, + the F3 fodder crop hay_grass = 14 species). A later slice refines it into a fine-grained one; a permissive 'unnamed remainder' would quietly become permanent. The 30 non-zero biomes are all named below (NavigableRiver by river_fish alone — see _comment_river_fish; its capacity_by_biome row is bypassed, so that host row means the FISHERY BONUS term, not the row); the 8 stated zeros (DeepOcean, HydrothermalVentField, SaltFlat, Glacier, ActiveVolcanoSlope, BasalticLavaField, AshPlain, FumaroleBasin) are named by nobody.
_comment_host_biomes: host_biomes IS A TABLE OF RELATIVE AFFINITY WEIGHTS, NOT CAPACITIES. A weight is meaningful only against the other weights on the SAME biome — 0.55 does not mean '0.55 of anything', it means 'more of this biome's basket than a species weighted 0.30 on it'. A species' best country carries its higher weight (date palm 0.55 on OasisBasin against 0.45 on HotDesertErg). NORMALIZATION IS WHAT MAKES NEUTRALITY STRUCTURAL: the engine divides each weight by the biome's total, so the shares sum to exactly 1 whatever anyone writes here. You cannot retune this table into a capacity change — the only thing a weight edit can do is move share BETWEEN the named plants of one biome. Retuning the human food web is a labor_config.json edit and must never ride in on a roster change.
_comment_yield: THE YIELD VECTOR — characteristic SHAPES of one per-species output vector, not separate subsystems. A harvest of B biomass pays B x yield.* into every account the species names: provisions (human food, the shipped forage path), fodder (animal feed) and MATERIALS (what the plant is made of — see _comment_yield_materials). TRADE_GOODS_PER_BIOMASS IS RETIRED (arc #527): it was written by every take site and read by nothing, while the materials block beside it credited the same take's concrete fibre and leaf. A cash crop is paid in materials now. `role` survives only as a DISPLAY TAG derived from which component dominates — it is never branched on in the sim. PROVISIONS_PER_BIOMASS IS NOW HAND-TUNED PER SPECIES AND LIVE (S1, docs/plan_flora_roster.md §4.3) — it was flat 0.05 verbatim in F1, and identical rates would have made every commitment pay the same. SINCE #433 EVERY RATE HERE IS LIVE AT EVERY RUNG: a patch converts at the SHARE-WEIGHTED AVERAGE of its own basket's vectors, so these numbers price a WILD tile too, not just a committed one — what is growing there decides what the tile pays. labor_config.json -> forage.provisions_per_biomass (0.05) is NO LONGER the wild rate; it survives as the empty-basket fallback and the rung-3 quality normalization baseline. Rung 2 then WEEDS (the favored share rises to min(1, share x tended_weeding_gain)) and multiplies THAT SPECIES' TERM ALONE by tended_conversion_gain — the favored-term-only rule is what makes the crop choice matter, since a blanket multiplier would pay the same for favoring anything. So the rates below are tuned so a good staple on its best country pays materially better than favoring a marginal neighbour on the same tile. Grains and tubers on their best ground are the strongest (wild_emmer 0.080 on AlluvialPlain); the gathered wild things sit at or barely above the 0.05 baseline (shellfish and river fish 0.050, pine nut 0.048, oak mast 0.045, arctic greens 0.040) — they are what you GATHER, not what you farm, and every one carries cultivation_ceiling `wild` so it can never be COMMITTED. THAT NO LONGER MAKES ITS RATE INERT (it did before #433): a wild-ceiling species is still weighted into its tile's basket average, so an oak-mast-heavy realization genuinely pays less per biomass than an emmer-heavy one and these numbers have to be right. fodder_per_biomass is 0.0 on every STAPLE row (grain is not feed) and LIVE since F3 on the one fodder crop, hay_grass (0.20) — a hay Field's harvest credits the band's FODDER store, a pen that knows Foddering draws it (see docs/plan_flora_roster.md §5). THE FIVE CASH CROPS (cotton, flax, tobacco, tea, grapevine) READ 0 IN BOTH SCALAR ACCOUNTS and are paid entirely by their materials rows, which is what keeps YieldVector::pays_something() true for them — a row paying into no account at all is rejected at load. PLAYTEST DIALS.
_comment_yield_materials: WHAT THE PLANT IS MADE OF (docs/plan_crafting_and_materials.md section 2) — the yield vector's third account (and, on a cash crop, its only one), and IT IS THE SAME BLOCK, character for character, that fauna_config's `hunt_yield.materials` carries and that a deposit's will carry. That is the point rather than a coincidence: a material is generic (there is no flax_fibre, there is Fibre), so nothing in the model may be plant-shaped or animal-shaped. AN OMITTED LIST IS THE ORDINARY CASE — most plants are food and nothing else — and unlike the three rate components there is no global to fall back to, because there is no species-blind statement of WHICH thing a plant gives. IT CANNOT BE AVERAGED ACROSS A BASKET the way the three scalars are: food and fodder are interchangeable numbers, a material carries a CHARACTERISTIC VECTOR, and averaging two species' would invent a plant that is not growing there. So a mixed tile's harvest DECOMPOSES into one credit per species, each keeping its own exact reading; credits that land in the same band merge in the band's store, which is where merging belongs. FIBRE IS THE ONLY CRAFTED MATERIAL THIS ROSTER GIVES — bast, boll, leaf and stem — and the two axes make 'there is no best fibre' real: cotton is fineness 0.92 EXCELLENT / strength 0.35 FAIR (a fine thread that will not hold), mesquite bast is 0.30 / 0.70 (coarse and strong), and neither is the upgrade. Hay straw (0.22 / 0.30) is the honest bottom of both. The rates are the plants humans actually retted, twisted and stripped: flax 0.06 and cotton 0.07 (a fibre crop is mostly fibre) against hazel bast at 0.010 (you take the bark off a shrub that is otherwise nuts). The three luxury crops (tobacco, tea, grapevine) give the UNCRAFTED materials tobacco/tea/grape instead - a producer exists, a craft does not; see materials.json's _comment_roster. Validated against materials.json at load, exactly as the fauna edge is. PLAYTEST DIALS.
_comment_cultivation_ceiling: HOW FAR UP THE PLANT LADDER A SPECIES CAN CLIMB — the exact twin of fauna_config.json's husbandry_ceiling, for the same reason. The ladder is a SEQUENCE (wild -> tended -> field), so a species' reach is a single ceiling and not two independent flags, which makes the incoherent 'sowable but not tendable' state unrepresentable (no validate() combination guard needed). `wild` is a gather-forever stand — an oak's mast is a wild harvest and you do not sow an oak forest on a five-turn horizon; `tended` reaches Cultivate but never Sow; `field` is the full ladder. Not every plant climbs, mirroring the manual's 'not every animal climbs'. LIVE SINCE S1: allows_cultivate()/allows_sow() gate which species a Cultivate/Sow assignment may COMMIT a patch to, and the auto-pick falls to the highest-share species the rung permits. A biome whose whole basket is `wild` therefore cannot be tended or sown at all (the open-water fisheries, the alpine peaks) — that is the ruling working, not a gap. reed_and_root is `field` rather than `tended` because it is the delta/marsh basket's only member: rice and taro on a river delta are the archetypal field crop, and leaving it at `tended` would have made the richest sowable ground in the game unsowable.
_comment_regrowth_rate: PER-SPECIES LOGISTIC REGROWTH — the plant twin of SpeciesDef.regrowth_rate. Every F1 row carries labor_config.json's forage.ecology.regrowth_rate (0.25) VERBATIM, so regrowth is unmoved along with everything else. Per-species divergence (a berry scrub that reseeds hot, a nut grove that does not) is a later slice.
_comment_river_fish: THE CHANNEL ITSELF, NOT THE VALLEY IT WAS CUT THROUGH. A navigable hex's forage capacity is TWO terms, not one (ForageLaborConfig::navigable_forage_capacity): capacity_for(underlying biome) + navigable_river_forage_bonus (80). The NavigableRiver row in forage.capacity_by_biome is vestigial and bypassed, so decomposing that row would name nothing that is actually there — and decomposing only the underlying biome would leave the whole 80-unit fishery UNNAMED, which is exactly the nameless food the coverage validator exists to forbid, leaking in through a path that validator cannot see. So this species is ALONE on NavigableRiver and means precisely the bonus term: a giant river is always a fishery. FloraConfig::navigable_composition blends the two baskets in the same two-term shape as navigable_forage_capacity (each weighted by ITS OWN term, then renormalized), and forage::tile_flora_composition is THE single seam every caller reads, so the capacity and the composition cannot drift.
_comment_realized_species: PER-TILE REALIZATION (docs/plan_flora_roster.md §10). The host_biomes weights above are AFFINITY — what CAN grow on a biome. What IS growing on a given TILE is a seeded subset: forage::tile_flora_composition draws realized_species_min..realized_species_max species (clamped to how many the biome hosts) by weighted sampling without replacement, keyed on (map_seed, tile), then renormalizes. So some alluvial tiles are wheat, others tobacco, instead of every tile carrying a diluted slice of all of them — and the rung-2 commit bar reads the tile's LOCAL realized share, which is what lets cash crops sit on AlluvialPlain without eroding wheat. PLAYTEST DIALS; validated 1 <= min <= max.

hay_grass._comment: THE FODDER CROP (Flora Roster F3, docs/plan_flora_roster.md §5). A fodder-DOMINANT species: its yield vector pays into the fodder account, NOT provisions (hay feeds animals, not people). `role: fodder` is a DISPLAY TAG derived from that dominance — the sim never branches on it; the vector does the routing (a hay Field's harvest credits the band's FODDER store, a grain Field's the FOOD store, through the SAME commodity-generic code). `cultivation_ceiling: field` because you SOW it — it is an ordinary rung-3 Field in every other respect (site rule, build, feral-if-abandoned). It hosts exactly the good sowable farmland (AlluvialPlain/Floodplain/RiverDelta/PrairieSteppe/RollingHills) so it COMPETES WITH GRAIN for the same scarce sowable tiles: calories OR herd-ceiling from one river-valley tile, the §4.3 land-use tension extended to the animal web. Adding it DILUTES the existing staple shares on those five biomes (the F1 normalization) — economy-neutral at the wild rung by construction (shares still sum to 1). SINCE #433 A WILD TILE READS THIS VECTOR TOO — a hay-bearing wild stand converts at its share of the 0.20, exactly as it does for provisions (see _comment_yield above); the older 'only a COMMITTED patch ever reads its vector' claim is superseded and was contradicting this file's own top-level comment. What an uncommitted patch does not get is the CREDIT: wild fodder is gated at the CONSUMER on the faction knowing Foddering (2007), at the credit site in systems/labor.rs and never in the rate seam, because crediting hay to a band with nowhere to put it hands out animal feed nobody bid for (docs/plan_flora_roster.md §4.3). `fodder_per_biomass` (0.20) is a PLAYTEST DIAL: it sets how much delivered graze-flow one unit of hay biomass is worth to a pen, and thereby how big a herd one hay field can carry (via the K_pen fodder term). Raise it for bigger fed pens, lower it if hay makes fodder the dominant strategy.

cotton._comment: A CASH CROP (Flora Roster F4, docs/plan_flora_roster.md 6). Paid in MATERIALS and nothing else: provisions_per_biomass is a SAFE, intended 0.0 (cotton is worthless as food - patch_species_quality divides by the WILD provisions rate, never the species rate, so a cash Field yields exactly 0 food with no divide-by-zero), fodder likewise 0.0, and the `materials` block below is the whole payoff. IT IS THE MATERIALS ROWS THAT KEEP YieldVector::pays_something() TRUE - the trade_goods scalar that used to do that is retired (arc #527), so a cash crop with no material rows would be rejected at load rather than silently producing nothing. `role: cash` is a DISPLAY TAG derived from that shape - the sim never branches on it; the vector does the routing (a cotton Field's harvest credits the band's material batches, a grain Field's the FOOD store, a hay Field's the FODDER store, through the SAME commodity-generic code). `cultivation_ceiling: field` because you SOW it - an ordinary rung-3 Field in every other respect. It hosts warm river-valley farmland (AlluvialPlain/Floodplain/RiverDelta) plus SemiAridScrub - HOSTED HONESTLY now that PER-TILE REALIZATION (10) dissolved the F4 dilution bind: some alluvial tiles realize as cotton while others realize as wheat. It COMPETES WITH GRAIN AND HAY for the scarce sowable tiles: calories OR herd-ceiling OR fibre from one river-valley tile, the sharp 'pays no calories' land-use tension. The fibre rate (0.07) is a PLAYTEST DIAL.

flax._comment: A CASH CROP (Flora Roster F4, docs/plan_flora_roster.md 6) - the cool-temperate-loam twin of cotton. Paid in MATERIALS: 0 food (SAFE - see the cotton comment), 0 fodder, and a fibre row that is the whole payoff. `role: cash` is a DISPLAY TAG; the vector routes, no role branch. `cultivation_ceiling: field` - a sown rung-3 Field competing with grain and hay for the scarce sowable tiles. Hosts AlluvialPlain/Floodplain (sowable) + RollingHills - honest hosting under per-tile realization (10). Flax fibre is 0.88 fineness / 0.80 strength against cotton's 0.92 / 0.35: THE PAIR IS THE POINT, not a rung ladder. PLAYTEST DIALS.

tobacco._comment: A CASH CROP (Flora Roster F4, docs/plan_flora_roster.md 6) - temperate, fertile, well-drained. Paid in MATERIALS: 0 food (SAFE - patch_species_quality divides by the WILD provisions rate, never the species rate), 0 fodder, and the UNCRAFTED material `tobacco` (arc #527). It paid the retired trade scalar and nothing else before that, so without this row it would produce literally nothing. `role: cash` is a DISPLAY TAG; the vector routes, no role branch. `cultivation_ceiling: field` - a sown rung-3 Field competing with grain and hay for the scarce sowable tiles. Hosts AlluvialPlain/Floodplain (sowable river-deposit ground, so the land-use tension lands) plus RollingHills/MixedWoodland. THE RATE (0.07) SITS WITH COTTON'S 0.07 AND FLAX'S 0.06 rather than with a byproduct like hazel bast's 0.010, because on a cash crop the harvested plant IS the product. The potency/keeping readings are PROVISIONAL PLACEHOLDERS for a luxury system that does not exist - see materials.json's _comment_roster.

tea._comment: A CASH CROP (Flora Roster F4, docs/plan_flora_roster.md 6) - a HILL/HIGHLAND crop, NOT lowland. Paid in MATERIALS: 0 food (SAFE), 0 fodder, and the UNCRAFTED material `tea` (arc #527), which is the whole payoff. `role: cash` is a DISPLAY TAG; the vector routes, no role branch. `cultivation_ceiling: field` - a sown rung-3 Field. Hosts RollingHills/MixedWoodland/HighPlateau - the upland/woodland baskets cotton and the grains do not reach, so tea is the cash crop of ground that grows little else. It is deliberately kept off the river valleys (no AlluvialPlain/Floodplain) so it is a genuinely different siting decision. The rate (0.06) matches flax's; the potency/keeping readings are PROVISIONAL PLACEHOLDERS - see materials.json's _comment_roster.

kelp._comment: Kelp beds & sea forests on the open shelf (Flora Roster F5, docs/plan_flora_roster.md §8). A wild-ceiling coastal gather at the baseline rate — you harvest a kelp bed, you do not farm it — so it thickens the shelf/coral baskets rather than adding a crop. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

sea_kale._comment: Sea kale & samphire — the salt-marsh greens of the tidal fringe (Flora Roster F5). Wild-ceiling: a shore gather at the baseline rate, breadth for the tidal/mangrove/shelf baskets. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

wild_rice._comment: Wild rice standing in the marsh & delta shallows (Flora Roster F5). A field-ceiling grain — the archetypal sown wetland crop, strongest on the freshwater marsh where it can dominate a small basket. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

cattail._comment: Cattail & bulrush rhizomes of the reedbeds and peat pools (Flora Roster F5). Tended-ceiling: a managed marsh stand. Rate lifted from the table's starting 0.055 to 0.069 to clear the per-realization commit bar: reed/berry/shellfish dominate all four of cattail's crowded wetland baskets, so its best realized share caps at ~0.5 and (share x tended_gain 1.5) x rate must still beat the wild 0.05 — needs rate > 0.0667. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

chestnut._comment: Sweet chestnut groves of the temperate woods and karst uplands (Flora Roster F5). Tended-ceiling mast crop — the woodland flagship's companion to hazel. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

wild_orchard._comment: Wild orchard fruit — crab-apple, plum, pear thickets of the woodland edge and hills (Flora Roster F5). Tended-ceiling. Rate lifted 0.060 -> 0.069 to clear the commit bar: both its baskets (MixedWoodland, RollingHills) are crowded, so its best realized share caps ~0.5. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

sunflower._comment: Sunflower & seedheads of the steppe and scrub (Flora Roster F5). Tended-ceiling oilseed gather. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

wild_pulses._comment: Wild pulses — vetch, lentil, chickpea ancestors of the grassland and silt (Flora Roster F5). Field-ceiling legume, the companion sown crop to wild emmer. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

mesquite._comment: Mesquite & acacia pods of the desert and badlands (Flora Roster F5). Wild-ceiling desert gather at the baseline rate — the arid biomes' own basket breadth. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

wild_fig._comment: Wild fig of the oasis and desert seeps (Flora Roster F5). Tended-ceiling. Rate lifted 0.060 -> 0.064 to clear the commit bar (best realized share ~0.55 against date_palm's dominance of the oasis). Starting affinity/playtest dial.

cloudberry._comment: Cloudberry & crowberry of the peat, tundra and taiga (Flora Roster F5). Wild-ceiling cold gather at the baseline rate — northern basket breadth. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

rock_tripe._comment: Rock tripe & lichen scraped from cold and stony ground (Flora Roster F5). Wild-ceiling famine gather at the LOWEST rate — the sparse cover of tundra, alpine, badlands and crater fields, what you eat when nothing else grows. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

alpine_herbs._comment: Alpine herbs & roseroot of the high meadows and plateaus (Flora Roster F5). Tended-ceiling highland gather. Rate lifted 0.055 -> 0.069 to clear the commit bar: pine_nut/seed_grasses dominate its highland baskets, so its best realized share caps ~0.5. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

cave_fungi._comment: Cave fungi cultivated in the cavern mouths and sinkhole shade (Flora Roster F5). Tended-ceiling — the subterranean anomaly biomes' own tended crop. Starting affinity/playtest dial.

grapevine._comment: Wild grapevine of the river valleys, oasis and hills (Flora Roster F5) - a CASH crop, the exact twin of cotton/flax: 0 food (worthless as food, patch_species_quality divides by the WILD rate so no divide-by-zero), 0 fodder, paid in the UNCRAFTED material `grape` (arc #527), which is the whole payoff. Field-ceiling; contests grain on sowable valley ground. GRAPE IS CURRENTLY DOMINATED ON BOTH ITS AXES by tobacco and tea, which sits badly against 'there is no best material' - recorded honestly rather than resolved, because a grape's value is entirely on the far side of a craft (fermenting) that does not exist. See materials.json's _comment_roster. Starting affinity/playtest dial.
